reason: French for perianth tube; the class is the existing FLOPO perianth tube.

A scape bract is a bract borne on the flowering axis below the inflorescence branches. That fits the PO definition of inflorescence bract. Some scape bracts are really leaf-like, so this is an approximation.

An epicalyx lobe is a lobe of a fused epicalyx, as in Malvaceae. It is not a separate bract. Mapping it to epicalyx bract loses the lobe and fusion meaning. The epicalyx is the safer bearer, or the rule should be rejected.
Same as R2453: the epicalyx lobe is part of a fused epicalyx, not a free bract.
The exostome is only the outer ring of a double peristome. Mapping it to the whole peristome loses 'outer' and mixes in the endostome. Reject, or add an exostome term.
The outer peristome is only the exostome part of a double peristome. Mapping it to the whole peristome loses that.
Exostome teeth are peristome teeth (PO_0030043, a single lobe of a peristome). They are not the whole peristome.
Endostome cilia are slender filaments between the endostome segments. They are not peristome teeth. No matching PO term exists, so reject.
Cilia of the endostome are filaments, not peristome teeth. No matching PO term exists.
An endostome cilium is a filament, not a peristome tooth. No matching PO term exists.
Rhizoidal tubers are tuber-like propagules on moss rhizoids. PO gemma is a small ball of cells on a thallus, so the two are different structures. Reject.
Rhizoidal tubers are tuber-like propagules on rhizoids, not PO gemmae. Reject.
Rhizoid tubers are tuber-like propagules on rhizoids, not PO gemmae. Reject.
A nectariferous scale is a scale that secretes nectar, which makes it a flower nectary.
A nectary disc is the nectar-secreting disc of the flower, so it is a flower nectary.
Spelling variant of nectary disc.
A nectariferous disc is a nectar-secreting disc, so it is a flower nectary.
Perichaetial leaves are the bracts around the archegonia. 'Perichaetal bract' is the PO term.
Plural of perichaetial leaf; same meaning as the PO perichaetal bract.
Spelling variant of perichaetal bract.

PO_0005656 carries 'gland' as a synonym, but 'basal' is a position. The rule drops it, and it only applies to glands at the base of a leaf, blade or petiole. Use the gland class with a position constraint, or reject.
Same as R2471: the position 'basal' is lost.
French for basal gland; the position 'basal' is lost.

Reticulate veins are leaf lamina veins only when the part is a leaf. Petals and bracts have reticulate veins too, and PO_0020138 is specific to the leaf lamina. 'Reticulate' is a quality of the vein, not part of the bearer.
Plural of reticulate vein; same constraint. The class fits only leaf veins.
Reticulate venation is the network pattern, not a vein. Mapping it to leaf lamina vein loses the pattern, which is the quality 'reticulate'. Handle it as a quality of the leaf venation.
Verticillaster is a listed synonym of cyme inflorescence in the PO lexicon.
Plural of verticillaster; same synonym.

A stigmatic branch is a branch carrying the stigma. Counts such as '2 stigmatic branches' do not mean two stigmas. PO has no stigma-branch term, so the rule loses the 'branch' meaning. Reject, or add a term.
French for stigmatic branch; counts and shape of branches would be recorded as stigma qualities.
Plural of the French stigmatic branch; same problem as R2480.
A stigma branch is a branch, not the stigma itself. Counts and shapes would be misattributed to the stigma.
A winter bud is a dormant bud, such as a turion or hibernaculum. Mapping it to bud loses that. Better to use bud plus a dormancy quality.
Plural of winter bud; the dormant, overwintering sense is lost.
A resting bud is a dormant bud. Mapping it to bud loses the dormancy meaning.
Reticulation is a pattern, a quality of a surface or venation (reticulate), not a part. It is not a leaf lamina vein. Seed or pollen surface reticulation is also covered by the word.
French reticulation is a pattern (a quality), not a vein.
The venation reticulum is the vein network. Mapping it to a single leaf lamina vein loses the network meaning. Reject, or treat it as the quality reticulate venation.
A style branch is a branch of the style, not the style itself. Counts such as '2 style-branches' would be recorded as style counts, and PO has no style-branch term.
Plural of style branch; same problem as R2489.
French for style branch; same problem as R2489.
Interprimary veins are a specific leaf-architecture vein class, lying between primary veins. Mapping them to any leaf lamina vein loses the order.
Plural of interprimary vein; the vein order is lost.
Intersecondary veins are a specific vein class, lying between secondary veins. Mapping them to any leaf lamina vein loses the order.
A secretory canal is a duct or space lined by secretory cells. PO_0005656 is the secretory tissue, so canal counts and sizes would be attached to the tissue.
Plural of secretory canal; the canal is a duct, not the secretory tissue.
French for secretory canal; the canal is a duct, not the tissue.
French plural of secretory canal; the canal is a duct, not the tissue.
A secretory duct is a canal, not the secretory tissue.
The PO comment says the area of alar cells is sometimes called the alar region. Descriptions of the region (colour, size, shape) are descriptions of the alar cells.
